rejectedAlternatives.internal: kept symbol-lease and patch-flow as internal authorities; rejected because both duplicate worktree isolation and one carries a hand-rolled WAL/lock subsystem
rejectedAlternatives.keepWithBaseline: would require new benchmark programmes; not needed once worktree isolation already covers the concurrency case

externalBasis.claim: Isolated git worktrees are the common industry answer to parallel coding agents writing the same files
Two agents in one checkout lose edits silently; worktree per agent plus review one diff per agent is the recommended shape
Lost writes in a shared working tree are expensive because they are unobservable by existing mechanisms
Worktrees are not a complete answer either: they share one .git, and lockfile edits still conflict across worktrees

components.rationale: A measured 4-process benchmark (12 wins / 36 denials, zero duplicate side effects) proves correctness but shows 75% of attempts are refused. That is throughput cost, and it adds no safety over isolated worktrees plus the merge queue.
